problem: The equation ${z}^{2}-25=-10z$ can be written in the form $(z+p{)}^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q.$

feedback.problem: The equation ${b}^{2}+14b+14=0$ can be written in the form $(b+p{)}^{2}=q.$   Find $p+q.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side and complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}^{2}+14b+14 & =0 \\ {b}^{2}+14b & =-14 \\ {b}^{2}+2\cdot 7\cdot b & =-14 \\ {b}^{2}+2\cdot 7\cdot b+{7}^{2}-{7}^{2} & =-14 \\ (b+7{)}^{2}-49 & =-14\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}(b+7{)}^{2}-49 & =-14 \\ (b+7{)}^{2} & =35\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $p=7,$ $q=35$ and $p+q=42.$
